ordered_diagnoses: Frontotemporal dementia and parkinsonism linked to chromosome 12

facts.raw_span: 6-month history of progressive dysarthria and dysphagia
Family history notable for a relative with memory problems after age 80
Cognitive impairment
Vertical gaze palsy
Tongue atrophy
Pyramidal signs
Severe loss of dopamine transporter binding in basal ganglia
Almost total loss in caudate nucleus
Left caudate: 0.35 (normal 1.55-2.07)
Heterozygous pathogenic variant of TBK1 gene (p.E643del) identified by whole-exon sequencing
Autoimmune encephalitis antibodies negative in serum and CSF
Large-amplitude, long-duration motor unit potential in frontalis, mentalis, orbicularis oculi, and genioglossus muscles

concepts.preferred_label: Frontotemporal dementia and parkinsonism linked to chromosome 12
concepts.why: The combination of progressive dysarthria, dysphagia, cognitive impairment, vertical gaze palsy, tongue atrophy, pyramidal signs, and severe loss of dopamine transporter binding in basal ganglia, along with a heterozygous pathogenic variant of the TBK1 gene, supports this diagnosis.
The presence of vertical gaze palsy, cognitive impairment, and severe loss of dopamine transporter binding in basal ganglia are characteristic of this disease.

The combination of progressive dysarthria, dysphagia, tongue atrophy, and large-amplitude, long-duration motor unit potentials, along with a heterozygous pathogenic variant of the TBK1 gene, supports this diagnosis.
The presence of cognitive impairment, vertical gaze palsy, and severe loss of dopamine transporter binding in basal ganglia, along with pyramidal signs, are characteristic of this disease.
The combination of progressive dysarthria, dysphagia, cognitive impairment, and a heterozygous pathogenic variant of the TBK1 gene, supports this diagnosis.

rationales.F03: Cognitive impairment is a key feature of frontotemporal dementia

rationales.F05: Tongue atrophy is a common feature of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis
rationales.F07: Severe loss of dopamine transporter binding in basal ganglia is characteristic of progressive supranuclear palsy
rationales.F10: The presence of a heterozygous pathogenic variant of the TBK1 gene is strongly associated with frontotemporal dementia and parkinsonism linked to chromosome 12
